title: Extension of left exact cover-preserving site functors to inverse images
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with finite limits, with a Grothendieck topology generated by a finite precoverage [def-weil-pbc-finite-precoverage, def-weil-pbc-topos], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a Grothendieck topos and put $H_U=h_U^\#$, the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,U)$. Write $\operatorname{LexCov}(\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$ for the category of functors $A:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ preserving finite limits and sending every finite covering family to a jointly epimorphic family; its arrows are all natural transformations. Restriction along $U\mapsto H_U$ is an equivalence from the category of finite-limit-preserving left adjoints $L:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal E$ to $\operatorname{LexCov}(\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$. The right adjoint to the extension of $A$ is the sheaf $R_A(G)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(A(U),G)$, and its left adjoint is canonically given by $L_A(F)=\varinjlim_{(U,s),\,s\in F(U)}A(U)$; an arrow $(U,s)\to(V,t)$ is $a:U\to V$ with $F(a)(t)=s$. In particular $L_A(H_U)\cong A(U)$, naturally in $U$. Every natural transformation of such site functors extends uniquely to their left adjoints, after these identifications. A finite-limit-preserving left adjoint with its right adjoint specifies a geometric morphism $\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism].

source.place: Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism), extended to a topos-valued functor using the canonical-site presentation in Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence) and the representable presentations Tags 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable) and 0GLW (lemma-colimit-representable). The explicit equivalence and transformation statement are an agent formulation, not a claim that 00X6 alone states them.

proof.text: Present $\mathcal E$ by a small sieve site, using its definition, and replace that presentation by a covering-family site $\mathcal S$ using [lem-trf-sieve-sheaves-covering-site]. Work in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)$. Starting with all $h_V^\#$ for $V\in\mathcal S$, all objects $A(U)$, and the terminal sheaf, close this set under chosen finite limits: at each successive stage adjoin the limits of every finite diagram in the full subcategory already obtained. Limits exist by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. The union over the nonnegative integers is a set and is closed under finite limits, since each finite diagram occurs at a finite stage; morphism sets are small since natural transformations are subsets of products of sectionwise function sets. Let $\mathcal D$ be the resulting full subcategory. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-subcategory-comparison], its jointly epimorphic families define a small subcanonical covering-family site and $N:\mathcal E\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$, with $(NG)(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(B,G)$. Choose the representative coverings to include the set of families $\{A(U_i)\to A(U)\}$ coming from the given finite covers. All sets, section values and element categories below are small in the containing universe of the statement; no colimit over the large category $\mathcal E$ is taken.

source.place: Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence), clauses (1)-(4), with its finite-limit closure construction; Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf).

proof.text: Corestrict $A$ to $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. Fullness and the construction of $\mathcal D$ show that $u$ preserves finite limits; its finite covering families are coverings in $\mathcal D$ by their specified joint epimorphy. The given finite precoverage is the covering-family site presenting the topology on $\mathcal C$; equivalently use its closure under the site axioms, which $u$ also preserves. Both $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ are small in the containing universe and all sheaves take values in its sets. For a sheaf $G'$ on $\mathcal D$ and a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ of $\mathcal C$, the family $\{uU_i\to uU\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal D$ and $u(U_i\times_UU_j)=uU_i\times_{uU}uU_j$, so the sheaf diagram of $G'\circ u$ at $\{U_i\to U\}$ is that of $G'$ at $\{uU_i\to uU\}$, an equalizer; thus $G'\circ u$ is a sheaf. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] gives $u_s=(u_p-)^\#\dashv u^s$ on sheaves of sets. Finite limits of sheaves are sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], $u_p$ preserves finite limits of presheaves [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] and $\#$ preserves finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], so $u_s$ preserves finite limits. Put $L_A=N^{-1}u_s$ and $R_A=u^sN$. Equivalences preserve limits and their inverse is both left and right adjoint, as follows by applying their Hom bijections to cones; hence $L_A\dashv R_A$ and $L_A$ preserves finite limits. The formula for $N$ in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-subcategory-comparison] gives $R_A(G)(U)=(NG)(uU)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(A(U),G)$, with restriction by precomposition; it is the sheaf $u^sNG$.

source.place: Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism) via Tag 00WX (lemma-adjoint-sheaves), applied after Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence); same-universe version, no tensor or abelian assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-sieve-set-sheafification-exists] and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], $\operatorname{Hom}(H_U,F)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_U,F)=F(U)$, naturally in $U,F$. Thus the adjunction in Step 2 gives, naturally in $G$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(L_AH_U,G)=(R_AG)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(A(U),G)$. The inverse natural Hom bijections evaluated at the two identity arrows give mutually inverse maps $L_AH_U\cong A(U)$. Naturality of the displayed bijections proves naturality of this isomorphism in $U$.

source.place: Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), combined with Categories Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda); the Hom calculation also appears in Tag 03A1.

proof.text: For $F\in\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ let $I_F$ have the objects and arrows in the statement, and let $s:H_U\to F$ be the map corresponding to $s\in F(U)$ by Step 3. These maps are a colimit cocone: for any sheaf $G$, a cocone $(b_{U,s}:H_U\to G)$ corresponds under the two cited Hom bijections to elements $x_{U,s}\in G(U)$ satisfying $G(a)(x_{V,t})=x_{U,F(a)t}$. These are exactly the natural transformations $F\to G$, by $s\mapsto x_{U,s}$, in both directions. This proves the colimit universal property directly, including its specified cocone, without presuming that $h_U$ is a sheaf or that $U\mapsto H_U$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 0GLW (lemma-colimit-representable), the category of elements and its displayed canonical cocone; universal property written out via Tag 00WH and Categories Tag 001P.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to $L_A$ and the small colimit cocone of Step 4. After the natural identifications of Step 3 its image has terms $A(U)$ and arrows $A(a)$, so it gives exactly $L_A(F)=\varinjlim_{(U,s)\in I_F}A(U)$. The colimit exists because this displayed image cocone is colimiting. For $f:F\to F'$ its structure map sends the leg indexed by $(U,s)$ to the leg indexed by $(U,f_U(s))$; this follows from the same equality for the canonical maps $H_U\to F$. Consequently the formula is natural in $F$ and specifies the same left adjoint as Step 2.

source.place: Tag 0GLW (lemma-colimit-representable), followed by Categories lemma-adjoint-exact: left adjoints preserve colimits.

proof.text: Let $L\dashv R_L$ and $M\dashv R_M$ be left adjoints and let $\alpha_U:LH_U\to MH_U$ be natural in site arrows. The adjunction and Step 3 identify $(R_LG)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}(LH_U,G)$ and $(R_MG)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}(MH_U,G)$. Precomposition with $\alpha_U$ defines a sheaf morphism $\beta_G:R_MG\to R_LG$, natural in $G$, because its components commute with all site restriction maps. Define $b_F:LF\to MF$ to be the $L\dashv R_L$ transpose of $F\xrightarrow{\eta^M_F}R_MMF\xrightarrow{\beta_{MF}}R_LMF$. Naturality of the units, adjunction bijections, and $\beta$ gives naturality of $b$. At $F=H_U$, the transpose of $1_{MH_U}$ evaluates at $U$ on the section corresponding to $1_{H_U}$ as $1_{MH_U}$. After $\beta$ it evaluates as $\alpha_U$, so $b_{H_U}=\alpha_U$. This identity uses arbitrary sections through the Hom bijections, without claiming a map of sheafified representables is a site arrow. For uniqueness, the colimit of Step 4 is preserved by $L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Every extension $c:L\to M$ satisfies $c_F L(s)=M(s)\alpha_U$ for every $s:H_U\to F$ by naturality. These colimit legs determine $c_F$ uniquely, and the constructed $b$ satisfies the same equation. Thus restriction is bijective on natural transformations and preserves their identities and composites.

source.place: Agent categorical argument from the universal properties in Tag 0GLW (lemma-colimit-representable), Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), and Categories Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Restriction is well defined. For a finite-limit diagram in $\mathcal C$, applying $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,-)$ gives its limit diagram of sets by the defining universal property, for every $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], $U\mapsto H_U$ therefore preserves finite limits. For a finite covering family $\{U_i\to U\}$, maps $H_U\to F$ correspond by the sheafification adjunction and Yoneda to sections of $F(U)$. Two such sections agreeing on every $U_i$ are equal by the sheaf condition. Thus $(H_{U_i}\to H_U)_i$ is jointly epimorphic by right cancellation. A left adjoint $L\dashv R$ sends this to a jointly epimorphic family: if $b,c:LH_U\to G$ agree on all $LH_{U_i}$, their transposes $H_U\to RG$ agree on all $H_{U_i}$, so are equal, and therefore $b=c$. Hence a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint restricts to an object of $\operatorname{LexCov}$. This proof also covers the empty covering family.

source.place: Tag 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), and the direct right-cancellation argument of lemma-covering-surjective-after-sheafification; covering epimorphy is proved here, not invoked as a new lemma.

proof.text: Step 6 proves full faithfulness of restriction, with all natural transformations as arrows. Steps 2 and 3 prove its essential surjectivity by the extension $A\mapsto L_A$. The isomorphisms of Step 3 supply its unit on objects; the comparison on any other left adjoint is the unique extension of its restriction-identification, invertible because the inverse identification also extends uniquely. They satisfy the equivalence identities by uniqueness. Finally $L_A\dashv R_A$ with $L_A$ preserving finite limits is a geometric morphism $\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ by [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. No choice of inverse site presentation changes the normalized extension, since Step 6 gives its unique comparison restricting to the identity on $A$.

source.place: Agent assembly from the preceding steps; geometric morphism means def-trf-geometric-morphism.
